# ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops Weekly Report (Aug 16 - 22, 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
This week focused on enhancing the operational stability and maintainability of the Superchain ecosystem through critical P2P networking fixes and performance validation. A major milestone was reached with the conclusion of SDM performance benchmarking, confirming no significant latency or resource impact under load. The team also prioritized infrastructure reliability by resolving long-standing connection flakiness between `op-reth` and `op-geth` and conducting essential operational rehearsals for signer management. While progress was made on codebase cleanup, the week was also characterized by intensive triage of complex race conditions in the interop and storage proof testing suites.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Network Stability & Interoperability
*   **P2P Connection Resolution:** Resolved a persistent issue involving peer-ID format mismatches between `op-reth` and `op-geth` in devstack. By normalizing formats and removing the `SKIP_P2P_CONNECTION_CHECK` workaround, P2P verification has been re-enabled for Rust E2E sysgo jobs ([#18570](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/18570)).
*   **Kona-node Configuration:** Finalized the architectural decision regarding `kona-node` L1 chain configurations. It was determined that base64 decoding of custom configs should reside within the deployment layer rather than the node itself, streamlining the node's internal logic ([#22491](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/22491)).

### Operational Maintenance & Governance
*   **Soneium Mainnet Updates:** Successfully updated the recipient addresses for all four L2 fee-vault predeploys (Sequencer, Base, L1, and Operator) to a new Safe address on Soneium Mainnet ([#1520](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1520)).
*   **Signer Management:** Conducted a rehearsal for the removal of a signer to ensure protocol readiness for governance-related security updates ([#1524](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/pull/1524)).
*   **Documentation & Cleanup:** Improved codebase maintainability by streamlining comments for FOS > FUS transfer tasks ([#1522](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/pull/1522)) and updating Sepolia execution hashes in the task documentation ([#1523](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/pull/1523)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **SDM Performance Benchmarking:** Concluded extensive testing which confirmed that SDM has no measurable impact on CPU, RSS, or latency, aside from a minor p99 PostExec delta ([#20176](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/20176)).
*   **Devstack Compatibility:** Closed the issue regarding `op-geth` support in devstack as the project shifts focus toward more modern stack configurations ([#18570](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/18570)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **Interop Test Flakes:** Significant effort is being directed at `TestSupernodeLightSequencerInteropInvalidMessageReplacement` ([#22234](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/22234)). Analysis revealed a race condition in the test's final assertions and a node-side "oscillation" behavior during recovery ([#21964](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/issues/21964)). A fix using a retrying DSL check is currently under review ([#22321](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/22321)).
*   **Storage Proof Indexing:** `TestStorageProofUsingSimpleStorageContract` was reopened due to a 30-second timeout flake. Investigations suggest the proofs indexing engine may be experiencing starvation or failing to advance past the genesis block on the validator EL ([#20376](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/20376)).
*   **PCD Benchmarking:** The `op-deployer` benchmarking issue ([#20916](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/superchain-ops/issues/20916)) remains active as existing TODOs in the code continue to trigger CI failures, indicating incomplete genesis-time-offset work.

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The week demonstrated a high level of technical coordination regarding the "Supernode Light Sequencer" interop tests. The collaboration involved splitting complex failures into distinct signatures (Signature A for assertion races and Signature B for cross-safe wedges) to allow specialized investigation. The decision to reject `MarkFlaky` annotations in favor of root-cause analysis highlights a strong commitment among maintainers to protocol-level stability over temporary CI suppression. Additionally, the operational rehearsals indicate ongoing synchronization between the DevOps and Governance teams to ensure secure Superchain management.
